text:
aditya: heads up — eu4 provisioning is stalled. Seen serial console flapping and BMC rate-limit errors on ~12 nodes in gpu-pool-7. Fleet API shows many nodes stuck at 'awaiting resources'. Notably, a BIOS/firmware push finished at 03:10UTC and 9 nodes reported Secure Boot toggled to ON. Can we pause that rollout and follow the revert runbook?

ops-bot: [ALERT] provisioner.high_error_rate — eu4/gpu-pool-7 — error 429 from mgmt-plane — 12 affected nodes (auto-throttle engaged) :rotating_light:

taylor: @aditya on it. pausing rollout now. Which runbook are you thinking? I can start a canary rollback if we want to be conservative.

aditya: revert runbook at https://go/redwood/runbooks/bmc-bios-rollback — prefer canary first. If Secure Boot is flipped, some OS install jobs are failing kernel verification and dropping to rescue.

jing: quick triage logs from one affected node (serial capture):

```
[   11.234567] Loading kernel… verification failed
[   11.234568] Secure boot: image not signed
[   11.234569] Dropping to maintenance shell
---
BMC: rate limit exceeded, retry later
IPMI: session closed by remote
```

jing: looks like nodes booted into the new BIOS which enabled Secure Boot by default. installer images aren't signed with the new key.

taylor: we have two immediate mitigation paths: 1) flip Secure Boot off on those BMCs temporarily, 2) roll BIOS back to previous image. Flipping via BMC is faster but messy for audit. Which is acceptable?

sre-oncall: prioritize keeping customer jobs running. Flip Secure Boot off for the impacted nodes to get them provisioning, then schedule BIOS rollback in off-peak window. Need owner for the flip — it's a privileged action.

aditya: I can own the flip for the 12 nodes. I'll run it in small batches (3 at a time) and monitor. Please prep a temp capacity plan in case some nodes fail post-flip.

taylor: commands to toggle via racadm/ipmitool (example, test on canary first):

```
# check current secureboot status
racadm getbiossetting -u admin -p $PASS "SecureBoot.Enable"
# to disable
racadm setbiossetting -u admin -p $PASS "SecureBoot.Enable" 0
# via IPMI (fallback)
ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P $PASS raw 0x3a 0x12 0x00
```

taylor: NOTE: exact racadm keys vary by vendor. ping me if your vendor refuses the setting. Also update the audit sheet: https://go/redwood/audit/bios-changes

jing: I'll watch serial/KVM outputs and the fleet API. If we see any nodes fail irreversible hw checks, we abort and fall back to reserving extra eu2 capacity.

sre-oncall: cost note — moving workloads to eu2 on short notice will add ~12% cross-region egress + spot upcharge for GPUs. Estimate ~$2.3k/day if we need to shift 150 GPU-hours. Approve temporary bump?

aditya: approve up to $5k/day for 24 hours if necessary. Try flip first.

taylor: started batch 1 (node-gpu-7-12/13/14) — flipping Secure Boot off now. Will post status in 5m. :eyes:

ops-bot: [AUDIT] aditya changed SecureBoot on node-gpu-7-12 — request id rc-8812 — reason: emergency-provisioning-mitigation

jing: batch 1 back to provisioning state, serial shows kernel passes signature check now. fleet-api transitioned node-gpu-7-12 -> provisioning -> ready.

aditya: batch 2 queued. Rolling windows: 3,3,3,3. Keeping 2 nodes as canary reserved.

taylor: filing a follow-up incident for root cause: BIOS image default toggles Secure Boot without gating. Need new preflight check that verifies installer signature compatibility before rollout. Ticket: INC-2026-1317.

sre-oncall: update runbook with extra safety: preflight list, and mark vendor-specific racadm keys. Also add a rollback path to previous BIOS image and an automatic capacity plan.

aditya: done — runbook updated and linked in ticket. Continuing batches. Will report back when all 12 are back to ready.

taylor: thanks. post-mortem to capture cost delta and decide if we should hold future BIOS pushes behind a canary in low-impact pools only. :memo:

ops-bot: [STATUS] Incident INC-2026-1317 created by taylor — summary: bios rollout enabled secure boot; 12 nodes in eu4 failed provisioning; temporary secureboot disable applied; rollback scheduled.

jing: all 12 nodes green as of 03:48UTC. Closing this thread unless new failures show up. :white_check_mark:
